title: The Casino of Lost Tuesdays
premise: A slot machine pays out in memories of work shifts never worked.
pressure: A slot machine pays in memories of Tuesday shifts the player never worked. Its attendant says nobody ever wins the same hour twice.
investigate: Compare the payout slips with old employee rosters
success: One slip gives a name and break time from an office that has never opened.
failure: The machine returns your coin and a vivid memory you cannot place.
help: Help the workers decide whether the machine should stay
helpOutcome: They vote for transparent odds and keep the impossible stories outside the payroll ledger.

title: The Bridge from the Other Side
premise: A stranger remembers crossing a bridge that was demolished before their birth.
pressure: A traveler recalls crossing a demolished bridge in childhood though the bridge fell before he was born. His photograph shows a vehicle with no driver.
investigate: Reconstruct the route from his photograph
success: The far bank holds fresh tool marks from a bridge that only exists at certain tides.
failure: The image fogs, but the traveler remembers the exact river bend.
help: Escort him across by the bridge people use today
helpOutcome: He reaches home without having to prove his impossible childhood to anyone.

title: The Banjo that Predicts Lightning
premise: A musician plays weather forecasts as bluegrass solos.
pressure: A banjo player's bluegrass solos predict thunderstorms with unnerving precision. A passing storm is missing from the county forecast.
investigate: Write down the notes and compare pressure readings
success: The tune names the exact road that will flood, note by note.
failure: A broken string ends the forecast early; the crowd still hears the warning cadence.
help: Help the musician alert neighbors without frightening them
helpOutcome: The little town makes practical storm preparations while the band keeps playing.

title: A Community Potluck for Cryptids
premise: A potluck has a strict no-photography policy and suspiciously good pie.
pressure: The cryptid potluck sign says NO PHOTOS; a neighbor with a camera says that policy proves criminal activity. The pies smell magnificent.
investigate: Ask the hosts to explain the rule in their own words
success: The seating chart is a map of secret wildlife corridors across the hills.
failure: A flash goes off and several guests vanish. The apology arrives on a napkin.
help: Respect the house rule and bring a dish
helpOutcome: The guests invite the suspicious neighbor to eat. They agree to keep names off the internet.

title: The Airport of Unscheduled Arrivals
premise: An aircraft lands with no engine noise and excellent snacks.
pressure: A silent plane lands at Kneeland with a passenger manifest listing people who have never been born. The pilot offers very good sandwiches.
investigate: Check the arrival notice without entering the aircraft
success: The destination stamp names a radio tower that is still a proposal.
failure: The passenger door shuts before you see the logbook, but a boarding pass remains in the grass.
help: Help the ground crew guide the aircraft safely
helpOutcome: Everyone clears the runway and nobody needs to climb aboard to prove the miracle.

title: The Amateur UFO Tow Truck
premise: Two neighbors offer roadside service for saucers stuck in mud.
pressure: Two neighbors advertise a tow truck for UFOs bogged down in Kneeland mud. Their client is smaller than the roadside warning sign.
investigate: Inspect the tow cable and claimed landing marks
success: You find a trail of unfamiliar metal shavings leading toward the county antenna.
failure: The cable snaps, proving only that the craft is heavier than it looks.
help: Organize a careful extraction without a spectacle
helpOutcome: The neighbors use planks and common sense. The driver departs after thanking the crew with a weather report.

title: The Fog That Followed You Home
premise: A personal patch of fog is politely but relentlessly attached.
pressure: A patch of fog follows you into a grocery store, queues politely, and makes the cashier's scanner read prices from another decade.
investigate: Measure its boundaries against the ventilation
success: The fog moves toward a receipt bearing the same lost-day date as an earlier clue.
failure: It changes shape every time you approach; the cashier writes down what the register said.
help: Ask the staff what would make everyone comfortable
helpOutcome: They open the doors and let the fog leave without treating frightened shoppers as fools.

title: The Midnight Cattle Crossing
premise: Cows follow invisible traffic signals with military precision.
pressure: Cows cross the road only at invisible green signals. Drivers honk at their patience and the herd refuses to hurry.
investigate: Look for the unseen traffic control
success: A roadside post transmits a sequence of pulses from an older county map.
failure: Your flashlight breaks the pattern and the herd waits until dawn.
help: Create a safe crossing with the rancher
helpOutcome: Volunteers hold traffic, and the cows pass without putting drivers or animals at risk.

title: Antenna for the Wrong Stars
premise: A ham-radio operator catches weather reports from an unfamiliar constellation.
pressure: A radio hobbyist receives a weather report for stars no observer can locate. The message ends with tomorrow's local wind speed.
investigate: Compare the transmission against multiple receivers
success: The same sequence comes from an abandoned county relay tower, not the sky.
failure: A battery dies before triangulation ends. You keep one clear call sign.
help: Share the recordings with independent listeners
helpOutcome: Three operators corroborate the signal and the hobbyist stops feeling alone.

title: Bigfoot's Custody Weekend
premise: Two Sasquatch parents ask the player to mediate a family logistics argument.
pressure: Two Sasquatch parents dispute custody of a muddy little backpack. The child is missing neither parent, only a schedule everyone understands.
investigate: Ask each parent what the child actually wants
success: A crayon map shows the safest trail between their separate homes.
failure: A shouted argument frightens the child into hiding, but the adults finally listen.
help: Help write a predictable handoff plan
helpOutcome: They agree on a familiar tree and both promise to show up without photographers.

title: The Museum's Escaped Footprint
premise: A plaster cast takes a midnight walk and leaves fresh tracks.
pressure: A plaster footprint escapes the museum and leaves wet tracks in the parking lot. The curator worries more about the donation ledger than the walking artifact.
investigate: Follow the fresh prints before they dry
success: They stop beside a sealed exhibit drawer containing the mold's second half.
failure: Rain smears the prints. The guard still witnessed the cast leave on its own.
help: Help the curator preserve the collection responsibly
helpOutcome: The museum labels the anomaly honestly and invites community review rather than selling a legend.

title: The Other Bigfoot Research Society
premise: Researchers have conclusive proof of tinyfeet and are furious nobody cares.
pressure: A research society has measured tiny humanlike footprints for years and resents every inquiry about Bigfoot. Its evidence cabinet is immaculate.
investigate: Examine the sampling method and site records
success: Their smallest footprint has a future date and a pattern matching the missing trail.
failure: A specimen cracks under the microscope; the researchers retain their original field notes.
help: Give the neglected team a fair audience
helpOutcome: They present their findings without demanding anyone believe a spectacular conclusion.

title: The River Claims a Witness
premise: A message in driftwood names a witness who was never present.
pressure: A river-carved message calls an absent witness by name. The witness lives nearby and claims never to have visited the bank.
investigate: Ask the witness to verify the driftwood's details
success: The wood records a flood stage not reached yet and a bridge support marked for repair.
failure: The carving fades in sunlight, but a photograph preserves the place.
help: Invite flood volunteers to inspect the shore
helpOutcome: They clear dangerous debris and begin a public watch of the vulnerable crossing.

title: A Cryptid's Online Dating Profile
premise: A woodland resident wants help writing a bio with less obvious fur-related clues.
pressure: A gentle woodland resident wants a dating profile that does not reveal its fur, feet or forest address. Every draft reads like a police report.
investigate: Ask what it actually loves instead of what it hides
success: The profile's ordinary details reveal a community garden the creature has quietly maintained.
failure: Its attempts at flirting collapse into weather forecasts. It learns a little honesty.
help: Help make a profile with boundaries and consent
helpOutcome: It posts a simple introduction without private coordinates and receives a thoughtful reply.

title: Mile Marker Zero and a Half
premise: A roadside sign changes distance whenever somebody lies.
pressure: A mile marker changes whenever a passenger tells a lie. The bus driver says it has been making the route longer every evening.
investigate: Check the sign while asking verifiable questions
success: A truthful answer restores half a mile and exposes a detour nobody authorized.
failure: The number jumps again when someone jokes, leaving a rough map but no explanation.
help: Help everyone reach the right stop anyway
helpOutcome: Passengers compare landmarks, settle the argument and arrive without making honesty a humiliation ritual.

title: The Hitchhiker Who Hitches Time
premise: A polite rider pays in gas receipts dated ten years ahead.
pressure: A hitchhiker pays with receipts for gas not sold until a decade from now. He knows the exit you were thinking of taking.
investigate: Ask where the receipts were printed
success: The paper carries an address for a depot planned in a county meeting next week.
failure: He leaves at the next turnout and the ink vanishes from the thermal paper.
help: Offer a safe ride without demanding his life story
helpOutcome: He makes it to town and leaves you a genuine thank-you written in today's date.

title: The Last Working Pay Phone
premise: An empty booth rings with calls from missing county offices.
pressure: A pay phone outside a shuttered store rings with calls from missing county offices. Each caller knows a different version of the road.
investigate: Keep a written log of the calls
success: Three offices describe the same public records room at different points in its future.
failure: The line goes dead before you can ask an address, but the number is printed on the handset.
help: Connect a caller to a real person who can help
helpOutcome: A retired clerk answers and discovers an ordinary records problem beneath the impossible messages.

title: The Alien Rest Area Review
premise: Visitors from elsewhere leave harsh customer-service ratings for Earth.
pressure: Alien travelers have rated the rest stop one star for hospitality, clean bathrooms and atmospheric gravity. The caretaker wants the reviews deleted.
success: One review contains a star chart with the exact route of tomorrow's suspicious plane.
failure: The translator gives every reply five stars and destroys the evidence of disagreement.
help: Help the caretaker make the stop welcoming
helpOutcome: Better signs and a working sink win a grudging second star from the guests.

title: The Logging Road to the Backroom
premise: A dirt road branches into a warehouse storing abandoned dreams.
pressure: A logging road ends at a warehouse stacked with boxed dreams. Each box has a name and a claim ticket marked UNCOLLECTED.
success: A receipt lists a community future that disappeared from last year's budget hearing.
failure: The boxes rearrange before you can read the account number. You keep a stamped stub.
help: Return one abandoned dream with its owner's permission
helpOutcome: A neighbor opens a box and remembers why they wanted to start a repair cooperative.
